questions.question_text: Before a South Dakota property manager performs any services, what must be in place?
questions.correct_answer: A written management agreement with the client
distractors: A verbal fee agreement confirmed by email
A copy of the owner's deed on file
SDREC approval of the management contract
questions.explanation: A property manager and client must sign a written management agreement specifying the duties and conditions of service before the manager performs any services (ARSD 20:69:14:06). Unlike an agency agreement, it may auto-renew if it allows written cancellation.

questions.question_text: A person wants to help tenants find apartments and collect a fee, but not manage properties. What SD license do they need?
distractors: No license is required for this activity
questions.explanation: A residential rental agent license covers negotiating residential rentals and collecting rents (SDCL 36-21A-12.1). The agent works under the direct supervision of a broker or property manager and may sign leases only if authorized, with the broker endorsing them.

questions.question_text: A property manager in South Dakota collects rental deposits. Where must these funds be held?
questions.correct_answer: In a properly designated trust account
distractors: In the property manager's personal account
In the property owner's bank account directly
In a separate escrow at the title company
questions.explanation: Security deposits, damage deposits, advance fees, and rents all go into a trust account at a federally insured institution (ARSD 20:69:14:11). Tenant security deposits are carried as a separate balance in the owner's ledger or a tenant ledger.

questions.question_text: Before a timeshare project can be sold to the public in South Dakota, it must be:
distractors: Approved by the local zoning board
Listed on the state MLS system
questions.explanation: Every time-share project must be registered with the commission annually before any interest is sold or advertised (SDCL 43-15B-2, 43-15B-3). Selling in an unregistered project is a violation the commission pursues directly.

questions.question_text: An investor personally owns eight rental houses, collects the rent, and signs the leases. Does she need a property manager license?
questions.correct_answer: No, a bona fide owner managing their own property is exempt
distractors: Yes, collecting rent always requires a license
Yes, unless she owns fewer than four units
No, but only if a licensed broker signs the leases
questions.explanation: The license law does not reach a bona fide owner or lessor performing these acts for property they own, or their regular employees (SDCL 36-21A-29(1)). Managing someone else's property for compensation is what triggers the license.
